skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Create Playwright-based web application tests for browser flows, forms, responsive layouts, network mocks, screenshots, and CI execution.
skill.summary: Build and improve Playwright tests for web application workflows, UI behavior, and cross-browser coverage.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: The static findings are explained by Playwright documentation, example test code, and local test-helper behavior. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, malicious command execution, or unauthorized upload intent was found in the reviewed context.

remediation.issue: Screenshot and video capture can record sensitive application data during real test runs.
remediation.suggestion: Document that tests should use sanitized accounts and restrict artifact storage for screenshots, videos, and traces.

remediation.issue: Examples use placeholder credentials and URLs that users might copy directly.
remediation.suggestion: Label all credentials and domains as placeholders and remind users not to commit real secrets or private URLs.

content.value_statement: Manual browser testing is slow and often misses regressions across forms, devices, and network states. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create practical Playwright tests for real web workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates Playwright test examples for navigation, forms, authentication, and shopping flows.
Shows browser, mobile device, viewport, screenshot, video, and trace configuration patterns.
Explains API mocking, request interception, and network monitoring for controlled tests.
Provides page object model examples for reusable test structure.
Includes setup, CI, and troubleshooting guidance for Python and TypeScript Playwright projects.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete generated test suite for every application.
Screenshots and videos can include sensitive data if tests run against real accounts.
Example URLs and selectors must be replaced with values from the target application.
Visual comparison examples are illustrative and need a real image comparison library.

use_cases.title: Add end-to-end coverage for a product flow
use_cases.description: Create Playwright tests for login, navigation, checkout, and success states before a release.

use_cases.title: Standardize QA automation patterns
use_cases.description: Use reliable selectors, fixtures, screenshots, and network mocks to reduce flaky browser tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare browser tests for CI
use_cases.description: Configure browsers, retries, traces, screenshots, and reports for repeatable pipeline execution.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic page test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright test for my home page. Check the title, main heading, and one navigation link. Use reliable selectors where possible.

prompt_templates.title: Test a form workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Playwright tests for this form flow: valid submission, required field errors, invalid email validation, and success confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Mock an API response
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright test that mocks the user profile API, verifies the rendered profile data, and confirms the API request was made.

prompt_templates.title: Design a full test strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Playwright test plan for login, checkout, mobile layout, visual screenshots, traces, and CI retries. Include risks and selector guidance.

output_examples.input: Test the login page with valid and invalid credentials.
output_examples.output: A concise Playwright test plan covering successful login, error messages, redirect checks, and session cleanup between tests.

output_examples.input: Add mobile coverage for the responsive menu.
output: Assertions for opened and closed states

output_examples.output: Recommendations to replace fixed waits with Playwright assertions, use stable selectors, isolate cart state, and capture traces on retry.

best_practices: Use test IDs, roles, and visible labels instead of fragile layout selectors.
Run tests against isolated accounts and sanitized data when screenshots or videos are enabled.
Prefer Playwright auto-waiting and assertions over fixed sleeps.
anti_patterns: Do not run browser tests against production accounts that contain sensitive data.
Do not store screenshots, videos, or traces in public artifacts without review.
Do not hardcode real credentials, secrets, or private URLs in test files.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps create Playwright tests for web pages, forms, authentication flows, mobile layouts, network mocks, and CI runs.

faq.question: Does it support Python and TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The materials include Python examples and TypeScript Playwright configuration patterns.

faq.question: Can it test mobile layouts?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows device presets, custom viewports, and responsive behavior checks.

faq.question: Can it mock APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for route interception, mocked responses, and request monitoring.

faq.question: Is screenshot capture safe?
faq.answer: Screenshot capture is useful for debugging, but artifacts should use sanitized data and restricted storage.

faq.question: Will it fix flaky tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns to reduce flakiness, but each application still needs targeted test review.
